cover.headline: Will Destinies Be Locked In This Week?
cover.dek: Oscar stands at the crossroads, with the Playoff Arena on one side and the Toilet Bowl on the other. Sean and Bob meet in the Game of the Week, Marissa chases the Emerald City, Shmoody digs for daylight, Tyler rides a goose into Mo’s snail army, and Tim and Abdo fish for .500. Week 10 predictions, analysis and Oscar’s picks.

games.title: Sean vs. Bob: Head This One, Sarge
games.lineText: (7–2) Sean - CEEEDEEEZZZZ nuts (−260) vs. (6–3) Bob - Shedeur Stay, Shedeur Go (+210)
games.spreadText: Spread: Sean −17 | Total: 286 | Projection: Sean 151.6 - Bob 134.6
story: Back in high school, on the varsity soccer field, Sean sent a cross into the box and Bob launched himself at it for a flying header goal. It was the best thing they ever did together. This Sunday Sean is serving up another cross, but this one has a timer on it, and it's set to go off in Week 10.

Sean is the No. 1 seed at 7–2 and has scored 1,327 points, the most in the league. A year ago he went 2–12 and finished last; now he's the title favorite at +130 with his playoff spot locked up. He's coming off 189.14 against Tim, the best score of Week 9. Joe Burrow (205 points), CeeDee Lamb (202) and Kenneth Walker (196) give him three of the best players on the field, and Brock Bowers is at tight end.

Bob is 6–3 and a game behind, with 97.9% playoff odds. Jaxon Smith-Njigba has 232 points, the most of anyone in this matchup, and is projected for 23.8. Brock Purdy and Kyren Williams are the rest of the core, and Drake London adds a second receiver who can win a week on his own. Bob has scored 140 or more in five games. He'll need another one, and probably 150.
It's the Game of the Week by a landslide: 4 of 6 manager votes. The fans haven't been kind to Bob either: all five fan picks are on Sean.

watch.text: 202 points and the best receiver in the matchup not named JSN. If he gets loose, the clock runs out on Bob.
232 points, a league-winner. He's the only player who can head this one back.

locker: I set him up once. Made him famous. This time I'm keeping the ball.
Sean always did his best work passing to me. Sunday he'll be watching me finish again.
games.oscarNote: Old teammates make the worst opponents, because each knows exactly where the other likes the ball. Oscar expects Sean's cross to land, just not on Bob's head this time.

games.theme: The Road to the Emerald City
games.title: Marissa vs. Tyriese: There's No Place Like the Playoffs
games.lineText: (5–4) Tyriese - No Love in The Land (+105) vs. (3–6) Marissa - Tuten on my Little Saq (−125)
games.spreadText: Spread: Marissa −3 | Total: 246.5 | Projection: Marissa 124.8 - Tyriese 121.9
story: The road to the Emerald City is paved in yellow brick, and the gates read PLAYOFFS. Marissa is on the road with a football under her arm and her dog at her heels. Standing in her way is the Wizard himself: Tyriese, in green robes, with the league's playoff picture in his crystal ball and a smile that says he already knows how it ends.

Marissa is 3–6, and her playoff odds are 9.5%. She's had 1,230 points scored against her, the third-most in the league, so the bad luck has followed her all the way down the road. But she's won two straight, including last week's upset of Hogies, 107.98–102.30. Drake Maye has 190 points, the most of anyone in this matchup, and he's projected for 23.2. Bhayshul Tuten, the man her team is named for, is projected for 16.3. Tetairoa McMillan and Garrett Wilson give her a solid receiver pair. A loss all but ends her season. A win keeps the Emerald City in sight.

Tyriese is 5–4 with 94.9% playoff odds. His 1,246 points are the third-most in the league, one point behind Mo. He's also won two straight: he beat Mo 166.98–147.66, then Shmoody 135.36–135.32 in the closest game in league history. The Wizard has the second-highest score this season, 180.34 in Week 5. His Bears are on bye, so D'Andre Swift and Caleb Williams sit this week. That leaves C.J. Stroud, James Cook and Tee Higgins to carry the magic.
Both teams lost players to byes this week, which is why the 246.5 total is the lowest on the board. The fans still believe in the Wizard: 4 of 5 fan picks are on Tyriese.

watch.text: 190 points and the best player on the yellow brick road. If he has a big day, she clicks her heels.
160 points. With the Bears on bye, the Wizard needs his top receiver to make the magic happen.

locker: I've been robbed every week by the schedule. Pay no attention to my record. Pay attention to Sunday.
Everybody comes to the Wizard eventually. Nobody leaves with a playoff spot.
games.oscarNote: The trouble with wizards is that, sooner or later, someone pulls back the curtain. Oscar thinks Marissa is the one who finally does it.

games.title: Collin vs. Hogies: Can Hogies Finally Get Collin to Shut Up?
games.lineText: (4–5) Collin - Annoyance of the league (+135) vs. (7–2) Hogies - White Tyriese (−160)
games.spreadText: Spread: Hogies −8 | Total: 250.5 | Projection: Hogies 129.3 - Collin 121.4
story: Every league has one, and the Villains have Collin. He wants to know your projected score before you've had your coffee. He leans over your shoulder to question your lineup. He hops in your Call of Duty lobby, plants a claymore, and stares at it. And when you're down, he asks, purely hypothetically, whether it's time to start talking toilet bowl. His team is literally named Annoyance of the League. This week the little brother gets Hogies, and Hogies has heard enough.

Hogies is 7–2, tied with Sean for the best record in the league, with 99.8% playoff odds. He's coming off a 107.98–102.30 loss to Marissa, his first game since trading away McCaffrey, and that's exactly the opening Collin has been waiting for. Hogies is a carpenter, and he builds his lineups the way he builds everything else: measure twice, cut once. Dak Prescott (172 points) and Trey McBride (163, the best tight end on the field) are the frame, and Chuba Hubbard and Chris Olave are projected for 17.9 and 16.4.

Collin is 4–5 with 27.7% playoff odds, and he's won two of his last three, over Tyler and Tim, before Bob beat him last week. He's scored 1,085 points, fourth-fewest in the league, and he hasn't topped 125 since Week 3. But he does have the best player in this matchup. Jahmyr Gibbs has 209 points and is projected for 24.7. Kirk Cousins has 180 at quarterback. If Gibbs goes off, Collin will be in Hogies' ear about it until Christmas.
The fans are with the carpenter: 3 of 4 fan picks are on Hogies.

watch.text: 163 points at tight end. He's the one who's been holding Hogies up all season, and that's no different this week.
209 points. He's the only reason Collin's mouth is still running.

locker: Hypothetically, if I win, does Hogies have to call me 'sir' in the group chat? Asking for me.
I've been on job sites with nail guns quieter than this kid. Sunday I'm putting a lid on it.
games.oscarNote: There is only one thing in the world worse than being talked about, and that is losing to the person doing the talking. Oscar expects Hogies to avoid both, but not quietly.

games.title: Zach vs. Shmoody: Escape from Toilet Bowl Penitentiary
games.lineText: (6–3) Zach - Trade God (−215) vs. (1–8) Shmoody - Team Shmoody (+175)
games.spreadText: Spread: Zach −13.5 | Total: 254 | Projection: Zach 133.6 - Shmoody 120.2
story: Welcome to Toilet Bowl Penitentiary. Guard Zach has his feet up, a box of donuts on the desk and a coffee mug with the prison's logo on it. Behind him, inmate #3027 is digging through the wall with a spoon. That's Shmoody, and here's the twist: he's last year's champion. He won the title in 2025, and nine weeks later he's in the toilet bowl's cell block.

Shmoody is 1–8 and has lost four straight. His playoff odds are 0.8%, and at +370 he's the third favorite to win the toilet bowl. But nobody in the league has been more robbed. He lost to Tyriese by 0.04 points last week, the closest game in league history, and to Hogies by 0.38 in Week 3. He's had 1,246 points scored against him, the most in the league. His only win came in Week 5, when he put up 147.78 on Sean, who is now the No. 1 seed. Bryce Young is projected for 19.5, and Derrick Henry and Nico Collins are both around 15. Puka Nacua, his top scorer with 174 points, has no projection this week, so the spoon has to do the work.

Zach is 6–3 with 97.5% playoff odds, and he's still the luckiest team in the league: only 1,020 points have been scored against him, the fewest of anyone. He lost his Smoke Boy Championship match to Mo last week, 122.36–118.46, so the guard is a little sore. Bijan Robinson (180 points) and Amon-Ra St. Brown (158) are projected for 19.9 and 19.5. Jayden Daniels and George Kittle are both over 16.
The fans are closer than the sportsbook: 3 fan picks are on Zach and 2 on Shmoody.

watch.text: 180 points. As long as he's running, the guard can keep eating donuts.
142 points. If anyone can break through a prison wall, it's King Henry.

locker: Dig all you want, champ. The only way out of here is through me, and I've got a 13.5-point head start.
I lost by 0.04 and 0.38. I'm not in here for being bad. I'm in here for being unlucky. This Sunday I'm out.
games.oscarNote: Every prison has one inmate who was framed, and in the Villains it's the defending champion. Oscar admires the spoon, but walls take time. Shmoody gets close, just not out.

games.title: Tyler vs. Mo: The Battle of Two Fools
games.lineText: (3–6) Tyler - Dolo’s cell mate (+455) vs. (4–5) Mo - Beazy (−640)
games.spreadText: Spread: Mo −32 | Total: 270.5 | Projection: Mo 151.3 - Tyler 119.3
story: The monks wrote it down in the margins, as they always do: in Week 10, King Mo leads his Snail Army toward the castle on the hill, the one marked The Playoffs. Charging the other way is Sir Tyler, in full armor, on the back of a war goose. A jester sounds the horn. The scribe has already titled the chapter "The Battle of Two Fools." The only question left is which one he meant.

Mo has the snails, but don't let them fool you. He's 4–5 and has scored 1,247 points, second-most in the league. He also holds the season's highest score, 196.1 in Week 5. He's the new Smoke Boy champion after beating Zach last week, 122.36–118.46. His playoff odds are 89%, and at +460 he's the second favorite to win the title. Josh Allen has 207 points, the most of anyone in this matchup, and is projected for 26.3. Ja'Marr Chase, Justin Jefferson and Malik Nabers give him the best receiver room in the league. The snail army moves slowly, but it doesn't stop.

Sir Tyler is 3–6 and has lost four straight. His 1,067.9 points are the fewest in the league, his playoff odds are 7.4%, and he's the toilet bowl favorite at +250. Last season he made it to the championship. This season the goose is doing most of the work. Jared Goff (18.8 proj), Jonathan Taylor (17.4) and Zay Flowers (16.4) are the knight's sword, shield and lance. The 32-point spread is the biggest on the board.
The fans have spoken: all 5 fan picks are on Mo.

watch.text: 207 points. The king doesn't ride into battle; he sends his quarterback.
154 points. If the goose is going to break through the snail lines, Taylor has to carry it.

locker: Laugh at the snails all you want. They've got Josh Allen, and you've got a goose.
Four straight losses and a 32-point spread. That's exactly when a fool on a goose takes down a king.
games.oscarNote: Oscar has always said that to lose one game may be regarded as a misfortune, but to lose four looks like carelessness. Tyler has a goose, a sword and a great deal of hope. Mo has Josh Allen. Oscar sides with Josh Allen.

games.title: Tim vs. Abdo: Who Reels In the Big One?
games.lineText: (4–5) Tim - The Coffey Shop (−205) vs. (4–5) Abdo - Beat the case (+170)
games.spreadText: Spread: Tim −12.5 | Total: 248 | Projection: Tim 130.2 - Abdo 117.8
story: Two anglers, one boat, one trophy bolted to the cooler. The water's rough, the lines are tight, and there's a fin circling under the hull. Tim is gritting his teeth. Baby Abdo, the youngest Shidid, is in his UFC hoodie, grinning like he's already got the big one hooked. Both men are 4–5, so whoever lands this one gets back to .500 and stays in the playoff hunt.

There's one complication: they're fishing in the same pond. Abdo's quarterback is Jordan Love (191 points), and Tim's top two receivers are Christian Watson (177) and Matthew Golden (164). All three play for the Packers. Every ball Love throws to them helps both men at once.

Tim has lost three straight, including taking Sean's 189.14 last week. He's still a 12.5-point favorite, because Trevor Lawrence is projected for 21.6 and Watson and Golden for 16.6 and 15.2. His playoff odds are 41%. The newlywed needs a catch to bring home.

Abdo is coming off his best game of the season: 152.98 against Tyler, when he sprang the trap. His playoff odds are 34.8%. Christian McCaffrey is projected for 22.1, the most of anyone in this game, and Tyler Warren is a reliable tight end. But Bucky Irving is on bye, so the receivers behind McCaffrey are thin.
The fans like Tim, 4 fan picks to 1.

watch.text: 177 points. If Jordan Love is going to throw a touchdown to someone, Tim wants it to be him.
167 points. He's the big fish under the boat, and Abdo has him on the line.

locker: Abdo's paying Jordan Love to throw touchdowns to my guys. Thanks for the bait, kid.
You're fishing. I'm fighting. Check the hoodie.
games.oscarNote: Fishing, like fantasy football, is mostly waiting for something you can't control. Oscar suspects Tim's line is stronger, and that Abdo will tell everyone the one that got away was bigger.

parlay.headline: McCaffrey reels it in
parlay.intro: One anytime touchdown from every team. Quarterbacks only count if they run one in. Last week: 4-for-12.
picks: 202 points and Sean's favorite target. Bob is guarding the header, not the slant.
JSN gets the yards. Kyren gets the goal line, which is where touchdowns tend to happen.
Her team is named after him. Oscar would feel terrible leaving him off the slip.
With the Bears on bye, the Wizard's magic runs through his top receiver.
The golden leg two weeks running. This week Oscar gives him the afternoon off from the gold, not from the slip.
He was on last week's slip too. The carpenter measures twice, and so does Oscar.
Everyone will take Bijan again. Oscar takes the receiver who catches everything in the red zone.
He's never once been stopped at the 1-yard line. Neither will the spoon.
Third straight week on the slip. One of these weeks the snails will carry him in.
The goose needs a touchdown, and Taylor is the only one on the roster who scores like it's his job.
Jordan Love throws to him whether Abdo likes it or not.
22.1 projected, the most of any leg on the slip. The big fish under the boat.
parlay.sign: McCaffrey is the golden leg, because a man projected for 22 points should score at least once. Tuten is the danger leg, because loyalty to a team name is not a strategy. Six receivers and six backs. Last week's slip went 4-for-12, which Oscar has decided to call a rebuilding year.

cover.headline: Race to the 1st seed
cover.dek: Sean's cross goes off on Bob, Hogies shuts Collin up, and the two leaders head down the stretch tied at 8–2. Tyriese wins by another hair, Shmoody breaks out of the toilet bowl penitentiary, Mo drops the week's top score, and Baby Abdo cashes in his briefcase on Monday night.
side: Neck and neck
Sean and Hogies are both 8–2. Sean has 1,487.94 points to Hogies' 1,348.86, so he keeps the top seed for now.
The chase pack
Tyriese, Bob and Zach are all 6–4. Tyriese leads that group on points (1,353.86), then Bob (1,335.16) and Zach (1,279.76). Zach didn't make the cover, and he's lost two straight.
Hair-splitter
Tyriese's last two wins came by 0.04 and 0.52, a combined 0.56 points.
Deadline week
The trade deadline is Week 11. Anyone chasing the top seed or running from the toilet bowl has one more week to make a move.

stories.headline: Bomb Squad: Sean's cross goes off, and Bob takes the blast
body: Oscar said on Thursday that Sean's cross had a timer on it, set for Week 10. It went off right on schedule. The sportsbook had Sean at **−17**, and all five fan picks were on Sean. Oscar picked Sean 149–136 and got the winner. Sean covered by 11.30, and the game went **7 points over** the 286 total.

The fuse was lit in the backfield. **Kenneth Walker was injured and out**, so Sean started another Chiefs back, **Emmett Johnson**, in his place. Johnson scored **35.10**, the most on the field. **Joe Burrow** added **33.16**, **CeeDee Lamb** had **20.20** and **DJ Moore** had **19.40**. Then the **Vikings D/ST** put up **22.00**, more than any of Bob's running backs.

Bob's top three showed up for the old high school reunion. **Brock Purdy scored 31.66**, **Jaxon Smith-Njigba scored 31.10** and **Deebo Samuel scored 25.90** from the flex. That's 88.66 points from three players. The other seven combined for **43.70**. Kyren Williams scored 5.20, Travis Etienne 6.40 and the 49ers D/ST 1.00.

Bob's bench made it worse. **Drake London scored 16.90** while Denzel Boston started and scored 2.60. **Alvin Kamara scored 16.40** while Kyren started. Those two swaps would have added 25.50 points, and Bob still would have lost by **2.80**. Sean wasn't perfect either: Ryan Flournoy scored 19.10 on his bench while Tucker Kraft started and scored 2.90. He didn't need it.
Sean moves to **8–2** and stays the No. 1 seed. Bob falls to **6–4**. Back in high school Sean set him up for the flying header. This time he handed Bob the ball and walked away before it went off.
locker: Walker went down, so they handed me the detonator. Thirty-five points. Boom.
Oscar picked Sean and got the winner. He called the cross with the timer, and for once the bomb went off exactly when Oscar said it would.

stories.headline: Ding dong, the season's dead: the Wizard drops a house on Marissa by 0.52
body: Last week Tyriese beat Shmoody by **0.04**. This week the Wizard needed a little more room and won by **0.52**. Marissa opened as a 3-point favorite, but the fans liked Tyriese 4 of 5. Oscar picked Marissa 126–121, and Oscar was wrong. With byes on both sides, the game went **32 points under** the 246.5 total.

The Wizard didn't have much magic left. His Bears were on bye, and every player on his bench scored 0.30 or less. Tyriese won with what he had: **James Cook scored 21.70**, **C.J. Stroud 20.44** and **Stefon Diggs 20.30**. **Tee Higgins**, Oscar's parlay pick, scored 11.60.

Marissa's season came down to the first quarter. **Drake Maye got hurt** and left with **3.02**. Meanwhile **Patrick Mahomes scored 35.42** on her bench, and once the game had started there was nothing she could do about it. Everyone else did their part. **Bhayshul Tuten**, the player her team is named for, scored **20.30**. **Cam Little** kicked his way to **19.00**, and the Colts D/ST added **15.00**. All of it fell 0.52 points short.

Tyriese has won three straight, and the last two came by a combined 0.56 points. He's **6–4** and nearly a lock for the playoffs. Marissa falls to **3–7**. The Emerald City is still out there, but the yellow brick road is mostly closed.
locker: Thirty-five points in sweatpants. Wrong week to be the backup plan.
Oscar said someone would pull back the curtain on the Wizard. Instead the Wizard pulled a house out of the sky. It's hard to argue with 0.52 points and a falling farmhouse.

stories.headline: Shut up, bot: Hogies finally puts a lid on Collin
body: The question all week was whether Hogies could finally get Collin to shut up. The answer is yes, for at least a week. Hogies closed at **−8** and covered by 6.14. The fans liked Hogies 3 of 4, and Oscar picked him 131–118 and got the winner. Nobody predicted the fireworks: the game went **63 points over** the 250.5 total.

Collin did not go quietly. **Jahmyr Gibbs scored 44.20**, and Oscar had warned that Collin would be in Hogies' ear about it until Christmas. **Tony Pollard added 23.90**, and Collin scored **149.68**, his best score of the season. On most Sundays that wins. **Germie Bernard scored 1.00** while Malachi Fields scored 9.20 on the bench, but that swap wouldn't have come close.

The carpenter built this one out of Dallas lumber. **George Pickens scored 43.50** and **Dak Prescott scored 34.42**, for **77.92 points** from one Cowboys stack. **Chuba Hubbard added 34.20** and **Jordyn Tyson 19.00**. Hogies had his own crooked nail: **Devin Singletary scored 0.30** in the flex while Elic Ayomanor scored 12.90 on the bench. He won by 14 anyway.

Hogies moves to **8–2**, tied with Sean for the best record in the league. Collin falls to **4–6**. He'll be back in the Call of Duty lobby this week, staring at his claymore, and hopefully a little quieter.
locker: Forty-three points. Tell the kid to put that in his group chat.
Oscar promised Hogies would win, but not quietly. Oscar has rarely been more right about anything.

stories.headline: Jailbreak! Shmoody digs out, and the whole league laughs at the guard
body: Oscar said the spoon would get close but not out. The spoon got out. Shmoody was a **+175** underdog with Zach giving **13.5**, and he won outright. Oscar picked Zach 133–125 and missed, and the fans picked Zach 3–2 and missed too. The last time anyone saw the guard, he was crying at a podium while the whole league pointed and laughed.

Shmoody's wall came down because of his receivers. **Parker Washington scored 28.20**, **Nico Collins 24.40** and **Blake Corum 20.90**. Puka Nacua sat on the bench with a zero, Bryce Young scored only 8.10, and it didn't matter. After losing by 0.04 and 0.38 earlier this season, the defending champion finally got a close one to go his way. His four-game losing streak is over.

The guard locked himself in again. Last week **Jadarian Price** scored 11.80 on Zach's bench and Zach lost by 3.90. This week **Price scored 11.40 on the bench** while **Demarcus Robinson scored 0.00** in the flex, and Zach lost by **3.18**. Two weeks, the same mistake, and a total of 7.08 points between Zach and two wins. **Amon-Ra St. Brown scored 25.80** and Jayden Daniels scored 20.76, but **Corey Kiner** scored only 2.50 and the **Ravens D/ST** scored 6.00 on Monday night.
Zach has lost two straight and falls to **6–4**. Shmoody is **2–8** and out of his cell. For now, at least, the toilet bowl's cell block is missing its most famous inmate.
locker: Two weeks in a row I'm sitting there with my helmet on. Coach, I'm right here.
Oscar admired the spoon and doubted the wall. Oscar apologizes to the spoon.

stories.headline: Mo torches the Chill Zone with the week's top score
body: The prediction called it the Battle of Two Fools, and by Sunday night it was clear which fool it meant. Mo was a **32-point** favorite, the biggest spread on the board, and all five fans picked him. Oscar picked Mo 148–122 and got the winner. Mo covered by 18.42, and the game went **24 points over** the 270.5 total. He didn't just cover. He brought a gas can.

Mo lit the place up. **Ja'Marr Chase scored 34.10**, **Isaiah Likely 27.70** at tight end and **Josh Allen 22.34**. **Justin Jefferson added 16.40**, **Quinshon Judkins 16.10** and **Ollie Gordon 15.50**, and the **Rams D/ST** put up **17.00**. Every Mo starter except Malik Nabers scored at least 7. His **172.64** was the best score in the league this week.

This has been building for a while. Mo started the season **0–4**. Since then he's **5–1**. Over his last four games he's **3–1** and averages **144.09 points**, and his only loss came when Tyriese scored 166.98. He beat Shmoody, then Zach for the Smoke Boy belt, and now Tyler by the most points of the week. He's .500 for the first time all season and looks like the team nobody wants to see in December.

Tyler's season has gone the other way. He was **3–2** after a 163.94 in Week 5. Since then he's lost **five straight**: 88.52 against Hogies, 122.32 against Collin (a loss by 2.48), 98.94 against Sean, 98.30 against Abdo and now 122.22. This week **Cam Skattebo scored 27.20** and **Jared Goff 20.42**, but Darren Waller scored 4.40, Jordan Mason 5.90 and Jordan Watkins 6.90. **Aaron Jones** (12.50) and **Antonio Williams** (12.20) both sat on the bench. Zay Flowers (11.40) and Tre' Harris (13.60) added 25.00 on Monday night, and it was nowhere near enough.
Mo moves to **5–5**. Tyler falls to **3–7**, and only Marissa has scored fewer points. The toilet bowl favorite is living up to his odds.
locker: Three weeks on Oscar's slip. This week I brought the matches.
Oscar said losing four looks like carelessness. Oscar doesn't have a word for five, so he'll just call it the Chill Zone.

stories.headline: Cash-in! Abdo opens the briefcase and steals it from Tim by 2.02
body: Abdo's team is called Beat the Case, and on Monday night he opened one. Tim was a **−205** favorite giving **12.5** points, and the fans picked him 4 to 1. Oscar picked Tim 128–119. Everyone was wrong except Abdo.

It came down to one running back on each side. Abdo led **104.60 to 101.08** going into Monday, with **Derrick Henry** left for Tim and **Omarion Hampton** left for Abdo. Henry ran for **19.00**, and Tim went up **120.08 to 104.60**. Abdo needed **15.49** from Hampton just to win. Late in the game Abdo trailed by 0.08, and Tim was already holding the belt over his head. Then Hampton finished at **17.50**, and Tim tapped out.

Abdo got there because of **Christian McCaffrey**, who scored **46.30**, the most of any player in the matchup, and cashed Oscar's golden parlay leg. Jonathan Taylor added 12.30 and the **Chiefs D/ST** added 10.00. The shared Packers pond Oscar warned about came up mostly empty. **Jordan Love scored 10.80**, **Christian Watson** 6.70 and **Matthew Golden** 12.00.

Tim did enough to win most weeks. **Chase Brown scored 28.30** and **Trevor Lawrence 26.78**. But **Konata Mumpfield scored 11.10** on his bench while Chimere Dike scored 4.10 and Hunter Henry 4.20 in the flex. One swap would have covered the 2.02.
Abdo has won two straight and is back to **.500** for the first time since Week 2. Tim has lost **four straight** and falls to **4–6**. The newlywed came home without the catch again.
locker: Everyone saw Derrick Henry and turned off the TV. I had the briefcase the whole time.
Oscar said the one that got away would be the story. He just thought Abdo would be the one telling it.

news.headline: Sean adds a bomb squad to the payroll
news.body: Sean has hired a full-time bomb squad and listed it on Sleeper as his D/ST. The league office has informed him that's not how it works. Sean says the Vikings D/ST scored 22 anyway, so he's keeping both.

news.headline: Hogies unscrews the Quiet Zone sign
news.body: With Collin finally quiet, Hogies took down his Quiet Zone sign and hung it in the trailer as a trophy. He's tied with Sean at 8–2 and has started measuring the top-seed banner, twice.

news.headline: Mo has the belt fitted for December
news.body: Mo is 5–1 since starting 0–4 and has taken the Smoke Boy belt to a tailor to have it fitted for the playoffs. The tailor asked what size. Mo said 172.64.

news.headline: Tyriese's margin of victory measured in microns
news.body: Tyriese's last two wins came by a combined 0.56 points. The league office has bought a jeweler's scale for his games. Tyriese says he doesn't need a big lead, just a little magic and a falling house.

news.headline: Sgt. Bob demands a bomb inspection
news.body: After the cross went off, Bob has asked the league office to inspect Sean's lineup for explosives. The inspector found a Chiefs backup running back and a Vikings defense. Bob is filing a second complaint about his own bench.

news.headline: Jadarian Price files a missing-person report
news.body: After scoring 11.40 on the bench for the second straight close loss, Jadarian Price has filed a missing-person report for his starting spot. The Trade God says he's looking into it and is open to offers.

news.headline: Abdo won't say what's in the briefcase
news.body: Abdo has carried the same green briefcase everywhere since Monday night. He's back to .500 and hasn't said a word about it. Sources say it ticks.

news.headline: Collin's vow of silence lasts one news cycle
news.body: Collin announced he'd be quiet for the rest of the week after scoring 149.68 and losing anyway. The announcement was 1,400 words long and was posted to the group chat at 2 a.m.

news.headline: Tim returns the championship belt
news.body: Tim was photographed holding a championship belt over his head on Monday night with 0.08 points to spare. He has since returned it to the store. The receipt says 'celebrated too early.'

news.headline: Marissa's get-well card for Drake Maye goes viral
news.body: After Drake Maye went down in the first quarter of a 0.52-point loss, Marissa sent him a get-well card the size of a garage door. Patrick Mahomes signed it from the bench, again.

news.headline: Shmoody's spoon goes to the Hall of Fame
news.body: The spoon Shmoody used to dig out of the toilet bowl penitentiary has been donated to the league's Hall of Fame. Shmoody is 2–8 but says the spoon is undefeated.

news.headline: Tyler's Chill Zone gets a fire inspection
news.body: After five straight losses and a 172.64 from Mo, the fire marshal has inspected Tyler's Chill Zone and found it 'extremely not chill.' Tyler has replaced the fire extinguisher with a smaller fire extinguisher.

parlay.headline: Oscar goes 6-for-12
parlay.golden: Golden leg cashes: Christian McCaffrey scored three touchdowns
parlay.note: CeeDee Lamb, Bhayshul Tuten, Jahmyr Gibbs, Amon-Ra St. Brown, Derrick Henry and Christian McCaffrey all scored. Gibbs, Amon-Ra and Henry scored twice, and McCaffrey three times. The danger leg, Tuten, cashed. Ja'Marr Chase caught 11 passes for 231 yards and somehow didn't score.
parlay.sign: Six of twelve. The golden leg scored three times, and Chase went for 231 yards without a touchdown, which Oscar is taking personally.

rank-2026-10.title: Race to the 1st seed
rank-2026-10.summary: Sean and Hogies are tied at 8–2 and hold the top two spots. Mo jumps three after the week's top score, Bob slides two after the bomb went off, and Shmoody digs his way out of last place. Tyler drops to 12th after his fifth straight loss.
rank-2026-10.note: Rank movement is calculated against the published Week 9 Gazette rankings. These are Oscar’s editorial power rankings, not official playoff seeding.

entries.take: Lost Kenneth Walker to injury and still scored 160.66, because his replacement scored 35.10. The most points in the league by almost 68 and the top seed. The bomb squad is fully staffed.
Pickens and Prescott scored 77.92 together, and Hogies scored 163.82, the second-best score of the week. Tied with Sean on record but 139 points behind him, so he needs help to get the top seed.
172.64, the top score of the week. He's 5–1 since starting 0–4, and he has the second-most points in the league. The record is only .500, but nobody wants this team in December.
Three straight wins, and the last two came by a combined 0.56 points. His whole bench was out or on bye, and he won with Cook, Stroud and Diggs. Lucky or magic, it counts.

Purdy, JSN and Deebo combined for 88.66, and the other seven scored 43.70. He had 25.50 points on the bench and would have lost even with a perfect lineup. Still a playoff team, just not a bye team yet.
Lost to a 1–8 team as a 13.5-point favorite, with Jadarian Price on the bench for the second straight close loss. Two losses by a combined 7.08 points. The Trade God has one week left to make a deal.
McCaffrey scored 46.30, and Hampton came through at the end on Monday night. Two straight wins and back to .500. The trade for McCaffrey keeps paying off.
Scored 149.68, his best score of the season, and lost by 14. Gibbs scored 44.20. With four games left, he needs this version of his team every week.
Lost by 2.02 on Monday night with Konata Mumpfield's 11.10 on the bench. Four straight losses, and this one hurt the most. The playoff window is closing.
Beat Zach outright as a big underdog, and the defending champion is out of last place. Parker Washington and Nico Collins combined for 52.60. He has more points than three teams with better records.
Lost by 0.52 after Drake Maye got hurt in the first quarter. Tuten and Cam Little did their part. She now has the fewest points in the league, and the playoff odds are close to zero.
Five straight losses. He scored 122.22 and still lost by 50 to the top score of the week. The toilet bowl favorite is earning it.

reports.headline: Coach Tyler opens a “Chill Zone” tent on the sideline, and your reporter refuses to enter it
body: Coach Tyler put up a tent behind the bench this week. Beanbags, a lava lamp and a little sign: CHILL ZONE. Inside, a fan blows on a bowl of oranges. In my day, the only place a man chilled was the ice bath, and he didn't enjoy it. Coach invited me in three times. I declined three times.

Carnell Tate and Jordyn Tyson, who arrived from Coach Hogies' crew on Tuesday night, would not go near it. They ran the blocking sled until it begged for mercy, then asked whether the tent could be moved so they had more sled room. Coach said the tent stays. Jared Goff went in, sat on a beanbag for one minute, came out and threw forty passes in a row without speaking. A man after my own heart.
Side field: Ladd McConkey (back, questionable) jogged laps around the tent. Terrance Ferguson and Jacory Croskey-Merritt, both on injured reserve, lay down inside it. That's the most use it's gotten.

quote.text: It's not a tent. It's a mindset.

reports.headline: Vlog: Coach Collin takes a vow of silence, and it lasts 41 minutes
body: Hey guys, welcome back to the channel! Huge one today. Coach Collin showed up with tape over his mouth and a dry-erase board around his neck that said “NOT TALKING THIS WEEK.” The whole team was SHOOK. He coached the first half hour completely by whiteboard: “run it again,” “nice,” “is Hogies watching?”

At minute 41 Jahmyr Gibbs broke a 60-yard run in team drills. Coach ripped the tape off and screamed “GET IN HIS EAR” at nobody. The vow is over. Smash that like button! Tony Pollard asked if he could keep the whiteboard. Coach said only if he writes his projected score on it every morning.

Side field: Sione Vaki (ankle) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) stood guard over the claymore. Brian Robinson Jr. (hamstring, injured reserve) says the claymore has moved two inches and he wants answers. Link in bio!

quote.text: Forty-one minutes. Hogies could never.

reports.headline: Coach seanwavy hires a real bomb squad to sweep the practice field, and they find the fog machine
body: FOLKS. Coach seanwavy brought in a FULL BOMB SQUAD this morning. Blast suits, a robot on treads, the works. They swept every yard of the field “for safety reasons.” Thirty minutes in, the robot found a suspicious device behind the bench. It was the fog machine. They detonated it anyway. ABSOLUTE SCENES. The groundskeeper wept.

Emmett Johnson had to carry the gold throne by himself this week while the squad cleared the 50. He did it in under a minute and then asked for a second throne. Joe Burrow threw to CeeDee Lamb through a cloud of what used to be fog. The Vikings defense showed up wearing blast suits they'd borrowed and wouldn't give back.
Side field: Kenneth Walker (groin) worked off to the side, and Brandon Aiyuk (knee) watched from a cart. The bomb squad waved to them on the way out.

quote.text: Sir, we don't usually detonate the fog machine.

reports.headline: Coach Hogies takes down the “Quiet Zone” sign. The job is done.
body: Monday morning, 6:58, Coach Hogies walked to the fence and unscrewed the QUIET ZONE sign with a cordless drill. Four screws. He didn't say a word. Then he hung it in the trailer next to the coffee pot, level to the bubble. Good craftsmanship is knowing when a sign has done its job.

A lumber truck rolled in from Dallas around nine. George Pickens and Dak Prescott unloaded it by themselves, two-by-fours on each shoulder, and stacked the whole load in under an hour. Chuba Hubbard built a set of stairs out of the leftovers just to see if he could. He could. Trey McBride checked every step with a level.

New hires Cam Skattebo and Zay Flowers reported Tuesday night and were handed hard hats before they got out of the truck. Side field: Josh Jacobs (finger) and David Montgomery (groin) sorted nails, and Romeo Doubs (shoulder, injured reserve) held the measuring tape.

quote.text: Measure twice, unscrew once.

reports.headline: I found a wizard robe in the equipment room. The team says it belongs to “the mascot.” The team has no mascot.
body: I got into the equipment room this morning. I won't say how. Behind the tackling dummies, hanging on a hook, I found a full-length blue robe with gold stars. A team spokesman told me it belongs to “the mascot.” I checked. This team has never had a mascot. Draw your own conclusions. I already have.

The smooth jazz played again, and James Cook ran the entire practice at exactly the tempo of the saxophone. C.J. Stroud threw to Stefon Diggs, who was at practice this time and seemed annoyed I'd noticed. Coach Tyriese stood on the 50 and stared at the sky for nine minutes. A man from the grounds crew said he was “checking the weather.” There wasn't a cloud in the sky.
Side field: Davante Adams (hamstring, injured reserve), Mike Evans (Achilles) and DeVonta Smith (hamstring). None of them would talk about the robe.

quote.text: It's a bathrobe. Please get out of the equipment room.

reports.headline: Undercover: the congregation holds a prayer vigil for Jadarian Price, who is standing right there
body: I got in this time disguised as a candle supplier. The Trade God's followers had ordered three hundred candles for a prayer vigil “for Jadarian Price's opportunity.” Price was standing in the middle of the circle the whole time, in full pads, holding a sign that said I AM RIGHT HERE. Nobody acknowledged him.

Coach Zach led the vigil from the bleachers, refreshing the trade block on both phones. The followers believe the deadline is a holy day. Amon-Ra St. Brown caught everything in the red-zone drill and had to step over candles to get back to the huddle. Bijan Robinson ran a perfect route, then knelt with the congregation out of politeness. Price lit his own candle.
Side field: Amon-Ra (ribs) and Luther Burden sat in the front pew between reps. TreVeyon Henderson and Jeremiyah Love, both on injured reserve, hummed the hymn.

quote.text: Faith is starting the right running back. We aren't there yet.

reports.headline: Coach Marissa sends Drake Maye a get-well card the size of a garage door
body: What a heartwarming morning! Coach Marissa wheeled a get-well card onto the practice field on a flatbed cart. It was the size of a garage door, with a gold glitter border and a drawing of Drake Maye riding a unicorn. Every single player signed it, the trainers too, and so did the kicker's mom, who happened to be visiting.

Patrick Mahomes ran the first-team offense and signed the card “Get well soon, buddy. I'll keep the seat warm.” Bhayshul Tuten ran the yellow line from the locker room to the end zone twice and then thanked the line. Cam Little kicked field goals from 50 until the sun went down and got a thank-you card from the goalposts.

Side field: Drake Maye, hurt Sunday, sat beside his giant card and looked moved. Garrett Wilson (concussion) and Adonai Mitchell (knee) did light work. Michael Wilson (neck) and Tank Bigsby (abdomen) are on injured reserve.

quote.text: We're a family, and this family has a lot of glitter.

reports.headline: The Coffey Shop installs a closing bell, and Coach Tim rings it 40 times
body: Tuesday rating: three beans. The shop installed a brass closing bell by the door this week. Coach Tim says it's so “everyone knows when the shift is over, and nobody celebrates early.” He then tested it forty times. The regulars have asked for earplugs.

Chase Brown worked the espresso machine and pulled twenty-eight shots before nine, a shop record. Trevor Lawrence handed out pastries again, and frankly he's become the face of the counter. Derrick Henry's King cup is now on a hook by the register, with a sticky note that says “fill all the way.” Konata Mumpfield wiped tables in the corner and asked whether he could work the front sometime. Coach said he'd think about it.
Side field: Jaylen Waddle (head) sat at the window table with a decaf.

quote.text: The bell rings at close. Not before. Never again before.

reports.headline: Coach Bob turns the film room into a boot camp and bans the word “cross”
body: There was no film on Tuesday. When the team arrived, the projector was gone. In its place was Coach Bob, in a camo jacket, with a whistle and a clipboard. He announced that the film room is now a training facility and that the word “cross” is banned from the building. A sign on the door says so. Jaxon Smith-Njigba asked about crossing routes. He did forty push-ups.

What followed was two hours of bear crawls, rope climbs and a drill Coach called “the obstacle course,” which was mostly the old VHS player and a stack of folding chairs. Brock Purdy finished first and was promoted to sergeant. Deebo Samuel ran the course twice and asked if there was a third. Drake London and Alvin Kamara were told to run it from the start line, not the bench.
Side field: Travis Etienne (hamstring), Denzel Boston (toe) and Jordan Addison (thumb) watched with their arms folded.

quote.text: Drop and give me twenty. And don't say the C-word.

reports.headline: Coach brought a briefcase. He didn't open it.
body: Coach Abdo walked in at seven with a green briefcase. Set it on the bench. Didn't open it. Nobody asked.

Christian McCaffrey ran the same drill sixty times and never got tired. Omarion Hampton waited until the last rep of practice to break one, then walked off without a word. Coach nodded at him once. That's two nods this season. Jordan Love threw to Tyler Warren and Caleb Douglas. The metal stayed loud.
At the end of practice Coach picked up the briefcase and left. A ball boy says it ticks. I believe him.
Side field: Lamar Jackson (thumb), Tyrone Tracy (hamstring) and RJ Harvey (knee), on injured reserve. A.J. Brown (knee) and Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle). Nobody talked there either.

quote.text: Later.

reports.headline: The hibachi chef throws a jailbreak party, and Parker Washington catches 14 shrimp in a row
body: The mood at the snack table has completely turned around. The hibachi chef set up a second grill, hung a banner that said FREE AT LAST and made an onion volcano shaped like a prison tower. When it erupted, the whole roster cheered. Ten out of ten. The chef cried a little.

Parker Washington caught fourteen straight shrimp, a new team record, and the chef gave him a ceremonial spoon in a glass case. Nico Collins caught eleven and asked politely for a second spoon. There's only one spoon. Blake Corum caught every shrimp Bryce Young threw to him, but Young threw most of them at the chef. Ashton Jeanty asked for steak again and was handed a shrimp.
Side field: Puka Nacua (knee, injured reserve) ate his shrimp from a lawn chair. Kyle Monangai (toe) and T.J. Hockenson (wrist) guarded the spoon.

quote.text: No walls in my kitchen. Only fire.

reports.headline: AND HERE COMES THE FIRE DRILL: Mo practices a two-minute drill with the building evacuated
body: LADIES AND GENTLEMEN, Coach Mohammed pulled the fire alarm at the start of practice, and he says it was on purpose. The whole building emptied onto the field, staff, trainers and the man with the clipboard, and Coach yelled “TWO-MINUTE DRILL, SAME SITUATION!” The offense ran it with three hundred people in the bleachers who had no idea what was happening. They cheered anyway. WHAT A SCENE.

Ja'Marr Chase caught a deep ball over the pool noodles and then helped the trainers out the door, a true gentleman. Isaiah Likely ran a perfect corner route through the evacuation line. Josh Allen threw eight straight completions while the fire truck pulled up. The Rams defense directed traffic. The Smoke Boy belt stayed on Coach the entire time and caught the light from the fire truck.
Side field: Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) helped hold the hose. Jonathon Brooks (abdomen) and Alec Pierce (heel), both on injured reserve, waved from the curb.

quote.text: Sir, there's no fire. Please stop pulling the alarm.

reports.headline: Coach Tyriese turns the practice field into a VIP section, and I have the receipts
body: There was a velvet rope at the 50, bottle service at the water cooler and a DJ booth in the end zone. Coach Tyriese calls it “team bonding.” I followed the money. He talked the stadium into the whole setup for free, and he got them to throw in a discount on the turf. This man could sell sand at the beach.

James Cook and D'Andre Swift ran their sprints to the beat. Tee Higgins wasn't allowed past the rope until he caught ten in a row. C.J. Stroud and Caleb Williams split the reps, and my source says Coach told each of them privately that he's the starter. On Sunday, one of them finds out he got sold.
Side field: Mike Evans (Achilles, questionable) worked the door at the rope. Davante Adams (hamstring, injured reserve) ran coat check.

quote.text: Practice ends at five. The after-party ends when I say it does.

reports.headline: Undercover: Coach Zach runs a soccer practice, and the drill of the day is the dive
body: I got in this week as a cone supplier. Coach Zach had the team in a rondo circle for the first hour, with no hands allowed. Then came the main event: diving. Players took turns falling to the turf at the slightest touch and grabbing their shins, and Coach scored each one out of ten for how much the referee would believe it. Amon-Ra St. Brown got a perfect ten. The referee is not on the payroll. I checked, twice.

The second half was an offside trap. Luther Burden and Rashee Rice stepped up in a perfect line while Jayden Daniels threw over the top. Late in the session, I spotted Coach behind the bleachers with a pair of binoculars pointed at Tyriese's practice field across the street. When he saw me watching, he smiled like a fox and ran another rondo.
Side field: TreVeyon Henderson (illness) and Jeremiyah Love (ankle), both on injured reserve, worked on their dives from a seated position.

quote.text: Football is just soccer for people who can't keep the ball on the ground.

reports.headline: Vlog: Coach Collin replaces the tackling dummies with memory foam, and he won't stop talking about it
body: Hey guys, welcome back! Today's practice was SPONSORED, kind of. Coach Collin swapped out every tackling dummy for a memory-foam mattress and spent twenty minutes explaining coil counts to the offensive line. Jahmyr Gibbs ran through three queens and a California king and asked if they came in firm. Coach said, “Everything comes in firm if you finance it.”

The water breaks went long, because Coach used each one for a fun fact. Did you know an octopus has three hearts? Tony Pollard does now. Did you know the shortest war in history lasted 38 minutes? Breece Hall timed the speech, and it ran longer than the war. Comment below if you've ever been to a practice with eleven water breaks!
Side field: Ray Davis (hamstring) and Sione Vaki (ankle), both questionable, tested the pillow-top. Brian Robinson Jr. (hamstring, injured reserve) has been asleep on it since Tuesday.

quote.text: You spend a third of your life asleep. Shouldn't you spend it on a Villains-certified mattress?

reports.headline: Coach Marissa is the first one in and the last one out, and she's put a “No Zach” sign on the gate
body: What a work ethic! Coach Marissa had the lights on at 5 a.m., the cones out by 5:15 and the playbook laminated by 5:30. She ran every drill herself, carried the water jugs herself and stayed after practice to re-chalk the yard lines. When an assistant offered to help, she thanked him and said she'd already done it.

The only interruption came at noon, when someone tried to slip into practice disguised as a cone supplier. Coach knew who it was right away. She walked him back to the gate and hung a sign on it: NO ZACH, NOT EVEN ON GAME WEEK. Patrick Mahomes said it was the most organized practice he's ever been part of. Travis Kelce asked how she puts up with that every day. Coach just smiled and went back to re-chalking.

Side field: Drake Maye (ankle) is out this week and cheered from a golf cart. Bhayshul Tuten (ankle) is questionable and did light work. Wan'Dale Robinson, Michael Wilson and Tank Bigsby are on injured reserve, and they folded towels.

quote.text: I've got a full-time job, a fantasy team and Zach. Only one of them gives me trouble.

reports.headline: Coach Tyler quizzes his players on their own stats, and the commissioner's phone never stops ringing
body: In my day, a coach blew a whistle and men ran. Coach Tyler shows up with a laptop, three spreadsheets and a pop quiz. Before stretching, every player had to name his own target share, red-zone touches and snap count from last week. Bucky Irving got all three right. Jared Goff asked if he could use a calculator. Coach said no, and told him the answer to two decimal places.

The trouble was the phone. Every ten minutes it buzzed with a commissioner problem: a vote dispute, a lineup lock, somebody asking why the website shows Week 10. Coach handled each one from the 40-yard line without missing a rep. The man knows more about fantasy football than anyone I've met, and it's a shame his record doesn't show it yet. New arrivals Carnell Tate and Jordyn Tyson got a forty-page scouting report on their own team.

Side field: Carnell Tate (shoulder), Jordyn Tyson (chest) and Ladd McConkey (back) are all questionable, and they studied the report from the bench. Terrance Ferguson and Jacory Croskey-Merritt are on injured reserve.

quote.text: I don't need luck. I need my projections to show up.

reports.headline: Coach Shmoody automates practice, and the snack table gets two-hour delivery
body: The snack table has been rebuilt by Coach Shmoody himself. He spent Thursday night installing a conveyor belt from the locker room to the 50, and now hibachi trays, Gatorades and footballs all arrive on it, sorted and labeled. Parker Washington got his shrimp in under ninety seconds. Ashton Jeanty ordered a steak and got it the same day. Nico Collins asked for a second spoon, and the system said it was out of stock.

Coach ran the rest of practice from a laptop in the bleachers, calling plays through an algorithm he wrote on his lunch break. It was the most efficient practice in the league, right up until Coach stepped behind the equipment shed for a “systems check.” A cloud came drifting over the field a few minutes later, and Bo Nix's spirals got noticeably more relaxed. The championship ring stayed on the whole time. It's the only thing from last year that still works.

Side field: Woody Marks (concussion) is out. T.J. Hockenson (wrist) and Jakobi Meyers (appendix) are questionable. Puka Nacua and Michael Pittman Jr. are on injured reserve, and they rode the conveyor belt for fun.

quote.text: Last year I built a champion. This year I'm building a better snack table.

reports.headline: AND THE TAKEDOWN! Coach Mo rolls out wrestling mats and makes the whole roster shoot doubles
body: LADIES AND GENTLEMEN, Coach Mohammed rolled out wrestling mats from sideline to sideline this morning and announced that nobody touches a football until they score a takedown on him. The man wrestled all four years of high school, and IT SHOWS. Josh Allen shot first and was on his back in four seconds. Justin Jefferson tried a single leg and got cradled. Ja'Marr Chase lasted eleven seconds, a new team record, and was rewarded with a juice box.

Then Coach did what Coach does: he grinded. He ran the two-minute drill, the red-zone drill and conditioning, then left for his day job at noon and came back at six to film every rep himself. Malik Nabers asked when Coach sleeps. Isaiah Likely said nobody has ever seen it happen. The Smoke Boy belt hung on the goalpost the whole time, and nobody was brave enough to touch it.
Side field: Jonathon Brooks (abdomen) and Alec Pierce (heel) are on injured reserve. They refereed from folding chairs and called everything for Coach.

quote.text: Wrestling taught me two things. Make weight, and never let a man up.

reports.headline: Coach Hogies brings the union to practice: 15-minute break, no exceptions, and Miller Lite at the final whistle
body: Coach Hogies ran this one like a job site in Midtown. Practice started at 7:00 sharp. At 10:00 he blew the whistle for a fifteen-minute break, and when Dak Prescott asked to finish the series, Coach said the contract is the contract. The new guys, Cam Skattebo and Zay Flowers, got their union cards, hard hats and a speech about how nobody on this crew does somebody else's job.

When it was time to work, they worked. George Pickens and Chuba Hubbard ran routes until the shadows were long. Trey McBride hauled tackling sleds like they were sheetrock. At the final whistle, Coach popped the cooler and handed everyone a Miller Lite. He said he's saving the last one for Sunday, so he can crush it when he takes the No. 1 seed.
Side field: Josh Jacobs (finger) is out this week and kept the time sheets. Romeo Doubs (shoulder, injured reserve) is the shop steward, and he filed two grievances about the Kingpin's scotch.

quote.text: Eight hours of work, eight hours of rest and eight hours of whatever I want. Sunday, I want first place.

reports.headline: Coach seanwavy runs a glow-up camp, and every player gets paid in $WAVY coin
body: FOLKS. Practice opened with skincare. Coach seanwavy set up a station at the 20 with face masks, a jawline trainer and a ring light, and nobody touched a ball until his skin was “game-ready.” Joe Burrow came out glowing. CeeDee Lamb got his dating-profile photos retaken in full pads and has three new matches already. Coach says confidence is the first thing he teaches. The second is your angles.

Every touchdown in team drills paid out in $WAVY, Coach's own cryptocurrency. Javonte Williams scored twice and is now worth either eleven thousand dollars or four cents, depending on the hour. Emmett Johnson asked how to cash out. Coach told him to hold, because it's going to the moon on Sunday night when the Kingpin locks up the No. 1 seed.

Side field: Kenneth Walker III (groin) and Brock Bowers (ankle) are both questionable, and they got the deluxe face mask treatment. Brandon Aiyuk (knee) is done for the season and is running the ring light.

quote.text: Look good, play good, buy the dip.

reports.headline: Sgt. Bob runs practice with a game controller, and the bye-week players play FIFA in the film room
body: With half his roster on bye, Sgt. Bob made a command decision. The players who aren't playing Sunday spent the morning in the film room in a FIFA tournament, with a bracket, seeding and a trophy. Jaxon Smith-Njigba beat Kyren Williams 4–1 in the final and celebrated by sliding on his knees across the carpet. Bob officiated in full uniform and handed out two yellow cards for rage-quitting.

The players who are playing Sunday got the real thing. Sgt. Bob called every play from the sideline through a headset with a controller in his hands: “Purdy, move up. Deebo, flank left. Godwin, hold the objective.” Then he ran a juggling drill to finish, because a sergeant who loves soccer doesn't let a practice end without one. Brock Purdy got to 14. Bob got to 212 and didn't break a sweat.
Side field: Jordan Addison (thumb) is out and kept score for FIFA. Dalton Kincaid (thumb) and Drake London (head) are questionable, and they watched the juggling from a folding table.

quote.text: Half my unit's on leave. The other half has a mission.

reports.headline: Coach Tim does the math, his wife does lunch, and the shop pours brewskis after close
body: Friday rating: four beans. Coach Tim showed up with a whiteboard covered in equations and explained the exact angle Trevor Lawrence needs to hit Rome Odunze on a deep post against Boston wind. Nobody followed it. Then Lawrence threw it, and it landed perfectly. The man is too smart for this league. Chase Brown asked if there'd be a test. Coach said Sunday is the test.

Coach is newly married, and it shows. At noon his wife came by with lunch for the whole team, and he walked her to the car and back twice. Derrick Henry got a homemade sandwich and has asked to be traded to nobody, ever. At close, the espresso machine went off and the tap went on. Coach poured everyone one brewski, just one, because he has a wife to get home to.
Side field: Jaylen Waddle (concussion) is questionable and sat at the window table with a decaf and the wedding photos.

quote.text: I solved the route tree on a napkin. I still don't know how Mo gets in my house.

reports.headline: Coach Abdo started a quarterback competition and didn't invite any quarterbacks.
body: Coach Abdo is 21. You can tell. He set up a quarterback competition, sent out a group text about it, then held it with no quarterbacks. Christian McCaffrey won. Coach posted the result to the league chat with a crying-laughing emoji and muted everyone who replied.

The rest of practice was mostly Coach on his phone, changing the team name to something new every hour to see who'd notice. Jonathan Taylor noticed. Coach changed it again. Omarion Hampton ran the last rep of practice to the end zone and spiked the ball at the press box. At me. Coach nodded. That's three nods this season.

Side field: Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle), A.J. Brown (hamstring) and Seth McGowan (hamstring) were out. Caleb Douglas (shoulder) and Matt Gay (hip) were questionable. Lamar Jackson and RJ Harvey are on injured reserve, and they're still waiting for the group text.

quote.text: lol

cover.headline: Welcome to Villains City
cover.dek: It's the trade deadline in Villains City, and every crew is turning up the heat. Sean and Hogies are both 8–2 and fighting over the same block, and the winner takes the top seed. Tyriese tries to pull a 17-point heist on Zach. Collin and Marissa meet in a back alley with their playoff lives on the line. Tyler and Shmoody fight a turf war over the toilet bowl. Bob shows up to face Abdo with half his crew on bye, and Tim tries to rob Mo's bank. Week 11 predictions, analysis and Oscar's picks.

games.title: Sean Wavy vs. Hogies: The Kingpin vs. the Usurper
games.lineText: (8–2) Sean - CEEEDEEEZZZZ nuts (−165) vs. (8–2) Hogies - White Tyriese (+135)
games.spreadText: Spread: Sean −8.5 | Total: 295 | Projection: Sean 151.8 - Hogies 143.2
story: The Kingpin is at his desk with his ring on and a drink poured, watching the security feeds. Cam 1 shows Hogies' convoy at the gate. It's the biggest game of the season: two 8–2 teams playing for the No. 1 seed, with only three weeks left after this one. The 295 total is the highest on the board. Whoever walks out of the mansion on Monday night runs Villains City.

Sean has run the place since Week 9. He has **1,487.94 points**, almost 68 more than anyone else, and he's won three straight. **Joe Burrow** (25.79 projected) and **CeeDee Lamb** (21.57) lead the crew, and **Javonte Williams** (21.06) gives him a second Cowboy. There are two cracks in the vault. **Kenneth Walker** (groin) and **Brock Bowers** (ankle) are both questionable. If Walker sits again, Emmett Johnson, who scored 35.10 the last time Walker was out, gets the call. With Tucker Kraft on bye, Bowers is the only tight end Sean has.

Hogies came to take the city. He held first place for a week back in Week 8, and he wants it back. On Tuesday night he made a move for weapons, getting **Cam Skattebo** and **Zay Flowers** from Tyler. Both debut on Sunday. **Dak Prescott** (21.66) and **George Pickens** (15.10) scored 77.92 together last week. Chris Olave, Chuba Hubbard and Trey McBride round out the crew. His kicker, Jason Myers, is on bye, so Hogies picked up Cairo Santos.

The Cowboys play on both sides of this one. Sean has Lamb, Javonte and Ryan Flournoy. Hogies has Dak and Pickens. Whoever gets more out of Dallas probably wins. The math is simple: if Hogies wins, he's 9–2 and takes the top seed. If Sean wins, he's 9–2 with a two-game lead in points, and the throne is close to locked.

watch.text: Questionable. If he plays, Sean has the best backfield in the game. If he doesn't, it's Emmett Johnson again.
He arrived on Tuesday night. If the new hire shows up, the convoy gets through the gate.

locker: I've been watching him on camera since Tuesday. He can bring the whole convoy. The gate's locked.
I built half the houses in this city. I know where the back door is.
games.oscarNote: Oscar has watched Hogies take the throne once, lose it a week later and spend two months building a ladder back up. The Kingpin should be nervous. Oscar suspects he isn't.

games.title: Tyriese vs. Zach: The Stick Up
games.lineText: (6–4) Tyriese - No Love in The Land (−255) vs. (6–4) Zach - Trade God (+205)
games.spreadText: Spread: Tyriese −17.5 | Total: 269.5 | Projection: Tyriese 143.6 - Zach 126.1
story: It's a normal day in Los Santos. Tyriese is walking down the block with his dog and his three-game winning streak, on his way to the playoffs. Zach is behind a tree with a knife. The Trade God has lost two straight, and it's deadline week, so he's out of patience and looking for something to take. The only problem is the dog.

Tyriese's problem this week is too many good options. **Caleb Williams** and **C.J. Stroud** are both projected for 20.37, so he has to pick one. **D'Andre Swift** (19.40) and **James Cook** (19.15) give him the best backfield in the game. **Tee Higgins** (18.55) and **Stefon Diggs** (13.33) lead the receivers. Mike Evans is questionable with his Achilles. Tyriese has won his last two games by a combined 0.56 points, so this week he'd like a little more cushion.

Zach is in trouble before he even swings. **Bijan Robinson, Jadarian Price and Corey Kiner are all on bye**, and his starting running backs are Emari Demercado (7.50) and Zonovan Knight (6.90). After keeping Price on the bench for two weeks, Zach now has no Price to start. Matthew Stafford is on bye too. What Zach does have is receivers. **Amon-Ra St. Brown** (18.93), **Luther Burden** (15.35) and **Rashee Rice** (15.27) can all hurt you, and **Jayden Daniels** (21.53) is the best-projected quarterback in the game. On Tuesday he traded Tyjae Spears to Collin for Kalif Raymond. Expect more phone calls before the deadline.

These two haven't met yet this season. Last year Tyriese went 9–5 and Zach went 7–7. Both are 6–4 now. Tyriese's playoff odds are 99.4%, and Zach's are 97%. Whoever loses still makes the playoffs, but the winner stays in the race for a bye.

watch.text: He's the dog on the leash. If Zach comes out from behind the tree, Swift bites first.
Zach's best weapon in a week with no running backs. For the stick-up to work, he needs a big day.

locker: I walk this block every day. He's been behind that same tree for two weeks.
Everything's for sale in Los Santos. Even the dog.
games.oscarNote: Oscar admires a man who brings a knife to a fantasy football game. Oscar admires a man who brings running backs more.

games.title: Collin vs. Marissa: The Yacht Heist
games.lineText: (4–6) Collin - Annoyance of the league (+100) vs. (3–7) Marissa - Tuten on my Little Saq (−120)
games.spreadText: Spread: Marissa −2 | Total: 251.5 | Projection: Collin 124.7 - Marissa 126.6
story: Every crew has a Lester, and in this league it's Collin. He's the mastermind who plans every job from a wall of monitors in his house, headset on, and never leaves. This week he did. After six days studying the blueprints for Marissa's yacht, *The Villains Queen*, he decided he couldn't trust anyone else with the job and went to do it himself. The safe is below deck, and it's heavily guarded, but it's not impossible to crack. Marissa is on the top deck with a glass of champagne and isn't worried. She calls the yacht a fortress. She also has a pistol. It's the closest game on the board, a 2-point spread, and the loser is close to finished.

Collin's crew is built around one man. **Jahmyr Gibbs** (23.54 projected) scored 44.20 last week and leads everyone in this game. **Tony Pollard** (15.26) and **Breece Hall** (12.37) back him up. Kirk Cousins (17.09) is now under center in Minnesota. His tight end, Harold Fannin, is on bye, so Chig Okonkwo (10.32) starts. Collin worked the waiver wire all week, adding Ray Davis and Pierre Strong and trading Kalif Raymond to Zach for Tyjae Spears. That's a lot of moves for a man who usually doesn't move at all.

Marissa's quarterback is no longer a question. **Drake Maye is out** with the ankle injury from Sunday, so **Patrick Mahomes** (22.59) starts with no backup plan behind him this time. **Bhayshul Tuten** (15.56) is questionable with an ankle injury, and **Saquon Barkley** (12.65) is ready if he can't go. **Tetairoa McMillan** and **Garrett Wilson** are both projected near 14.7, and **Travis Kelce** adds 12.74.

There are seven playoff spots, and right now Abdo has the last one at 5–5. Collin is 4–6 with 33.6% playoff odds. Marissa is 3–7 at 3.7%. The loser is probably done, and the winner keeps the heist going. The fans like Collin 4–1. The sportsbook likes Marissa by a field goal.

watch.text: He's the safecracker. If Gibbs gets loose, Collin walks out with the safe.
No more getting comfortable on the bench. He's the security system now.

locker: I studied the blueprints for six days. I know where every camera is.
games.oscarNote: Oscar has always said the mastermind should stay home. The first time Lester leaves the house in years, he goes straight to a yacht with an armed woman on it.

games.title: Shmoody vs. Tyler: From Championship Glory to Rock Bottom
games.lineText: (3–7) Tyler - Dolo’s cell mate (−140) vs. (2–8) Shmoody - Team Shmoody (+115)
games.spreadText: Spread: Tyler −5 | Total: 236.5 | Projection: Tyler 120.9 - Shmoody 115.8
story: Welcome to Liberty City. Last December these two were the two best teams in Villains Fantasy. They wore suits to the 2025 championship game, and each of them held a trophy while the photographer took the picture. Shmoody won. Tyler finished second. Eleven months later, the mansion has a REPOSSESSED banner on it, both cars are on a tow truck, and the former finalists are sitting on the curb next to a sign that says WELCOME TO THE TOILET BOWL. Last year they owned the city. This year they can't afford the bus.

It's a rematch of last year's title game with nothing at stake but pride and a bad trophy. Tyler is **3–7** with five straight losses and 2.9% playoff odds. Shmoody is **2–8** at 0.4%. The fans like Shmoody 4–1. The sportsbook likes Tyler by 5. Whoever loses takes over last place in the power rankings, and probably the inside track to the toilet bowl too.

Tyler rebuilt the roster this week with his whole bus fare. **Bucky Irving** (17.11) and **Jonah Coleman** (17.02) lead the backfield, and **Jared Goff** (16.95) is barely ahead of new pickup Cam Ward (16.87) at quarterback. The receivers are the problem. **Carnell Tate** (13.01), **Jordyn Tyson** (10.85) and **Ladd McConkey** (11.99) are all questionable. Tate and Tyson came over from Hogies on Tuesday night, so Tyler's playing a lot of people who just got to Liberty City. He also picked up Mark Andrews to play tight end.

Shmoody pawned the quarterback. He dropped Bryce Young and picked up **Bo Nix** (17.90) and Aaron Rodgers. **Nico Collins** (16.05) and **Parker Washington** (14.29), who scored 52.60 together last week, are the reason he got off the curb. **Ashton Jeanty** (12.01) and **Sam LaPorta** (12.12) fill in. Puka Nacua is still on IR, and Woody Marks is out with a concussion. The defending champion's run of bad luck finally broke last week. Now he wants to see if he can start a streak.

watch.text: The one thing Tyler hasn't sold for bus fare. If he goes off, the streak ends.
He's the reason the spoon got Shmoody out of the cell. He needs one more good week.

locker: Last year I lost the championship to this man. This year I'll settle for beating him in the parking lot.
I still have the trophy. It's the only thing they didn't repossess.
games.oscarNote: Oscar remembers when these two wore suits. Oscar would like to remind both men that no one remembers who won the toilet bowl, only who ended up in it.

games.title: Mo vs. Tim: The Trevor Visit
games.lineText: (4–6) Tim - The Coffey Shop (+375) vs. (5–5) Mo - Beazy (−510)
games.spreadText: Spread: Mo −30 | Total: 265.5 | Projection: Tim 117.6 - Mo 147.8
story: Tim tried to retire. A few weeks ago he changed his title to "Assassin (retired)," and lately he's been living the quiet life in Vinewood: a new wife, a pool, a drink in his hand, and four straight losses he'd rather not talk about. Then a beat-up pickup pulls into the driveway. Mo hangs out the window with blood on his tank top and a gas can on the passenger seat, yelling, "TIM!!! You really thought you could have a quiet season?!" Nobody invited Mo. Nobody ever does. He shows up anyway, and then the house explodes.

Mo is the most dangerous man in Los Santos right now. He went 0–4, then 5–1, and last week he scored **172.64**, the top score in the league. He's .500, holds the Smoke Boy belt and has 96.3% playoff odds. **Josh Allen** (24.46 projected) leads, and **Ja'Marr Chase** (21.52), **Justin Jefferson** (18.47) and **Malik Nabers** (16.20) make up the best receiver room in the league. **Isaiah Likely** (14.85) is at tight end. The only thing missing is a running back. Quinshon Judkins and Rhamondre Stevenson are on bye, so Jaylen Warren (14.76) and Ollie Gordon (11.11) get the carries. That's the biggest spread of the week, **Mo −30**. All five fans picked Mo.

Tim's house was already on fire before Mo pulled in. His Packers, **Matthew Golden and Christian Watson**, are both on bye, and so are Kyle Pitts and Konata Mumpfield. That leaves him starting **Michael Mayer** at tight end and Laquon Treadwell at receiver. **Trevor Lawrence** (20.57) is the best player he has left. **Derrick Henry** (15.29) and **Chase Brown** (14.80) give him a real backfield, and **Rome Odunze** (11.38) is his top receiver. Jaylen Waddle is questionable with a concussion. Tim's playoff odds are 30.2%. A fifth straight loss probably ends the season.

watch.text: If Tim wants his quiet life back, his quarterback has to put the fire out by himself.
He brought the matches last week. Mo brought the gas can this week.

locker: I didn't come over for a drink, Tim. I came over because I was bored.
I'm retired. I have a pool. Please leave.
games.oscarNote: Oscar has never seen a man retire successfully in this league. Oscar has also never seen Mo leave a party before something was on fire.

games.title: Bob vs. Abdo: The Five-Star Manhunt
games.lineText: (6–4) Bob - Ahmed is still muted (+380) vs. (5–5) Abdo - Beat the case (−520)
games.spreadText: Spread: Abdo −30.5 | Total: 207.5 | Projection: Bob 88.5 - Abdo 119.0
story: Sgt. Bob has the radio in one hand and the map in the other. "This is Bob. We have Abdo on the move. I repeat, Abdo is armed and running. All units converge." Baby Abdo has his arm out the window and his foot on the gas, with five stars on his wanted level and a helicopter overhead. He's won two straight, he's back to .500, and he holds the last playoff spot. Bob has the whole force behind him. He just doesn't have many officers who are actually on duty this week.

Half of Bob's force has the week off. **Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Drake London, Kyren Williams, KC Concepcion, Denzel Boston and DeMario Douglas** are all on bye, and Jordan Addison is out. That's most of the team that's carried him to 6–4. Bob spent the week calling in reinforcements: **Chris Godwin**, Xavier Hutchinson, Samaje Perine and kicker Jason Sanders. **Brock Purdy** (17.83) leads what's left, with **Dalton Kincaid** (9.51, questionable), **Deebo Samuel** (8.86) and **Travis Etienne** (8.72). Bob is projected for 88.5, the lowest on the board. He's still at 98.2% playoff odds, so this is a manhunt he can afford to lose.

Abdo is armed, but he doesn't have a quarterback. **Jordan Love is on bye and Lamar Jackson is on IR**, so he'll need someone off waivers before Sunday. He does have the best player in the game: **Christian McCaffrey** (19.99 projected), who scored 46.30 last week. **Jonathan Taylor** (14.33) and **Omarion Hampton** (10.26) give him three real running backs, and the **Chiefs D/ST** (12.33) is the best defense in the matchup. Omar Cooper, Caleb Douglas and Matt Gay are all questionable. Abdo's playoff odds are 38.2%. Collin, Tim and Mo are all within a game of him, so every week now is a chase.

San Francisco is on both sides of this one. Bob has Purdy, Deebo and the 49ers D/ST. Abdo has McCaffrey and Keenan Allen. It's the biggest spread of the week, **Abdo −30.5**, and the lowest total at 207.5. The fans like Abdo 4–1.

watch.text: The last officer on duty. If anyone is going to catch Abdo, it's the 49ers quarterback.
The getaway driver. He outran Tim last week, and now he has to outrun the whole department.

locker: Six of my guys are on vacation. I'm calling in the National Guard.
games.oscarNote: Oscar has watched Sgt. Bob walk past a claymore, guard a soccer goal and survive a bomb. Oscar would like to point out that chasing a man in a car is harder when half your squad car is empty.

parlay.headline: Gibbs goes for gold again
parlay.intro: One anytime touchdown from every team. Quarterbacks only count if they run one in.
picks: The Kingpin's favorite target, in a Cowboys game with the No. 1 seed on the line.
Forty-three points last week. The convoy goes through Dallas.
The dog on the leash. He bites at the goal line.
No running backs means the ball goes to the receivers. Oscar takes the one who scores.
The safecracker, and the most-projected player on the slip.
Mahomes needs someone to throw to, and Oscar likes the big target in the end zone.
The one thing Tyler hasn't sold for bus fare.
He caught 14 straight shrimp at practice. Oscar trusts his hands.
One of the few officers still on duty. He might have to score it himself.
The getaway driver. He always finds the end zone.
With the Packers on bye, Tim needs the King to carry the whole house.
Everyone expects Chase. Oscar takes the fourth receiver in the best receiver room in the league.
